doc78.summary: De Puebla tells Almazán that people around the Princess of Wales, for their own interest, had her write the letters he encloses; that he sees her household finely dressed beyond expectation; and that the greed of certain persons is such that he doubts even the treasure of [?the King of England] would content them. Written as Philip and Juana were about to sail from England; Katharine's own letter of the next day (CSP I no. 459) says her people were all but naked.
doc78.en:
ll. 18-20: [...] those people brought it about, for their own interest, that the princess wrote me these letters,
which go enclosed here. [...]

ll. 24-25: I see the lady princess's people so finely dressed that I did not think to see more.

ll. 25-27: [?For] the greed of certain persons [?] [?] is such that, even with [?the] treasure of {the King of
England?}, I doubt they would be [?content] [...]

l. 29: [...] is going along at the mercy of chance (a beneficio de natura) with this [...]

system: Puebla's First Cipher: a letter substitution with homophones for a, b/v, c, e, i (Tomokiyo's reconstruction of Bergenroth's key no. 6), with one Great Roman Numeral code group (DCCCLXXXVIII, el Rey de Inglaterra); cipher passages set inside clear text.
